description: Experience the vibrant flavors of authentic Chinese Hot and Sour Soup, a comforting bowl renowned for its invigorating balance of tangy vinegar and fiery white pepper. This classic recipe combines tender pork, silken tofu, and earthy mushrooms in a rich, savory broth, creating a truly satisfying culinary delight. It is a hearty and flavorful soup perfect for any season, bringing warmth and a delightful kick to your palate.

instructions.title: Prepare Ingredients
instructions.text: Rehydrate dried shiitake and wood ear mushrooms in separate bowls of hot water for 20-30 minutes until softened. Drain, squeeze out excess water, remove shiitake stems, and thinly slice both types of mushrooms. Slice pork tenderloin, firm tofu, and bamboo shoots into uniform matchsticks. Prepare the cornstarch slurry by mixing cornstarch with cold water in a small bowl.

instructions.title: Simmer Broth Base
instructions.text: In a large pot or Dutch oven, bring chicken broth to a boil over medium-high heat. Once boiling, reduce heat to a simmer and stir in the light soy sauce, dark soy sauce, and white pepper. Allow it to gently simmer for 5 minutes to combine flavors.

instructions.title: Add Main Ingredients
instructions.text: Add the sliced pork tenderloin, rehydrated mushrooms, firm tofu, and bamboo shoots to the simmering broth. Stir gently and cook for about 5-7 minutes, or until the pork is fully cooked through and the vegetables are tender-crisp.

instructions.title: Thicken the Soup
instructions.text: Give the cornstarch slurry a quick stir to re-mix it, then slowly pour it into the simmering soup in a thin stream, stirring constantly to prevent lumps. Continue stirring until the soup thickens to your desired consistency. This usually takes about 1-2 minutes.

instructions.title: Add Egg Ribbons
instructions.text: Once the soup is thickened, reduce the heat to low. Slowly pour the beaten egg into the soup in a thin, continuous stream while stirring the soup in a circular motion with a ladle or chopsticks. This creates delicate egg ribbons throughout the soup. Cook for about 30 seconds until the egg is set.

instructions.title: Finish and Serve
instructions.text: Remove the pot from heat. Stir in the rice vinegar and toasted sesame oil. Taste and adjust seasonings, adding more white pepper or vinegar if desired for a stronger hot and sour kick. Ladle the soup into individual bowls, garnish with sliced scallions, and a drizzle of chili oil if you prefer extra heat. Serve immediately.

tips: For an authentic flavor, do not skimp on the white pepper; it provides the signature 'hot' element, distinct from chili heat. Add it gradually to your preference.
If you cannot find dried wood ear mushrooms, fresh shiitake mushrooms can be used instead, though the texture will be slightly different. Rehydrating dried mushrooms yields a deeper umami.
Hot and Sour Soup is best enjoyed fresh. If reheating, do so gently to avoid breaking down the egg ribbons and to maintain the soup's thickened consistency.
article:
The tantalizing aroma of a robust broth, the vibrant dance of flavors, and a satisfying warmth that envelops you – these are the hallmarks of great Chinese cuisine. Among the vast array of culinary treasures, one soup stands out for its bold personality and universal appeal: Hot and Sour Soup. This iconic dish, a staple in Chinese restaurants worldwide, is celebrated for its intricate balance of piquant heat and tangy sourness, creating an unforgettable sensory experience. Whether you’re seeking comfort on a chilly evening or a flavorful start to a multi-course meal, Hot and Sour Soup delivers a symphony of tastes that awakens the palate and satisfies the soul.

## What is Hot and Sour Soup?

Hot and Sour Soup, or *Suan La Tang* in Mandarin, is a classic Chinese soup known for its distinctive flavor profile. Originating from Sichuan province, it masterfully combines spicy and sour elements, creating a warming and invigorating dish. The "hot" typically comes from white pepper and sometimes chili oil, while the "sour" is primarily derived from black vinegar. Beyond these defining characteristics, the soup is rich in textures, featuring tender slivers of meat, often pork, and a medley of ingredients like bamboo shoots, wood ear mushrooms, tofu, and scrambled egg ribbons, all suspended in a thickened, savory broth. It's a dish that stimulates every taste bud, offering a complex yet harmonious blend that has captivated diners for generations.

## Ingredients for Hot and Sour Soup

Crafting an authentic Hot and Sour Soup requires a thoughtful selection of ingredients. Here's a comprehensive list to guide you:

For the Broth:
*   6 cups chicken or vegetable broth (high quality makes a difference)
*   2 tablespoons soy sauce (light or regular)
*   2 tablespoons Chinese black vinegar (Chinkiang vinegar is ideal for its rich, aromatic tang)
*   1-2 tablespoons white pepper (start with 1, add more for extra heat)
*   1 tablespoon sesame oil
*   1 teaspoon sugar (to balance the flavors)
*   Salt to taste

For the Solids:
*   4-6 ounces pork loin or tenderloin, thinly sliced into matchsticks (can substitute with chicken or omit for vegetarian)
*   4 ounces firm or extra-firm tofu, pressed and cut into small matchsticks or cubes
*   1/2 cup dried wood ear mushrooms (or cloud ear mushrooms), rehydrated and thinly sliced
*   1/2 cup dried shiitake mushrooms, rehydrated, stems removed, and thinly sliced
*   1/2 cup bamboo shoots, drained and thinly sliced into matchsticks
*   2-3 dried red chilies (optional, for extra heat and aroma)

For Thickening:
*   3 tablespoons cornstarch
*   4 tablespoons cold water (to make a slurry)

For the Egg Drop:
*   2 large eggs, lightly beaten

For Garnish (Optional):
*   Chopped green onions
*   Fresh cilantro
*   Chili oil

## Step-by-Step Instructions

Making Hot and Sour Soup at home is a rewarding experience. Follow these steps for a delicious bowl:

1.  **Prepare the Ingredients:** If using dried mushrooms, rehydrate them in warm water for at least 30 minutes until soft. Drain, squeeze out excess water, remove shiitake stems, and thinly slice all mushrooms. Slice pork, tofu, and bamboo shoots into uniform matchsticks. Prepare your cornstarch slurry by whisking cornstarch with cold water until smooth. Beat the eggs lightly in a small bowl.
2.  **Cook the Pork (Optional):** In a large pot or Dutch oven, heat a tablespoon of oil over medium-high heat. Add the thinly sliced pork and stir-fry until it's just cooked through and no longer pink, about 2-3 minutes. Remove the pork from the pot and set aside.
3.  **Build the Broth:** Pour the chicken or vegetable broth into the same pot. Add the rehydrated mushrooms, bamboo shoots, and tofu. If using, add the dried red chilies. Bring the mixture to a simmer over medium heat.
4.  **Season the Soup:** Once simmering, add the soy sauce, Chinese black vinegar, white pepper, and sugar. Stir well to combine. Taste and adjust seasonings as needed; you might want more vinegar or white pepper depending on your preference for "hot" and "sour." Add salt if necessary.
5.  **Thicken the Soup:** Give the cornstarch slurry a quick stir (it separates quickly). Slowly pour the slurry into the simmering soup in a thin stream, stirring continuously to prevent lumps. Continue stirring until the soup thickens to your desired consistency. If you want it thicker, you can mix a little more cornstarch with water and add it gradually.
6.  **Add the Egg Drop:** With the soup at a gentle simmer, slowly drizzle the beaten eggs into the soup in a thin stream, stirring gently in one direction with chopsticks or a fork. The eggs will cook instantly, forming delicate ribbons.
7.  **Finish and Serve:** Stir in the cooked pork (if using) and the sesame oil. Remove the dried red chilies if you don't want them in the final serving. Ladle the Hot and Sour Soup into bowls. Garnish with chopped green onions and fresh cilantro, and a drizzle of chili oil if desired.

## Tips for the Best Hot and Sour Soup

Achieving that perfect balance in your Hot and Sour Soup involves a few key considerations:

*   **Quality Ingredients Matter:** Use a good quality chicken or vegetable broth as it forms the foundation of your soup. High-quality Chinese black vinegar (like Chinkiang) is crucial for the authentic sour tang.
*   **Balance is Key:** The beauty of Hot and Sour Soup lies in its equilibrium. Don't be afraid to taste and adjust the white pepper and vinegar throughout the cooking process. Add a little at a time until it's just right for your palate. A touch of sugar helps round out the flavors and prevent the sourness from being too sharp.
*   **Don't Over-thicken:** Add the cornstarch slurry gradually while stirring. You want a velvety consistency, not a gloopy one. You can always add more, but you can't easily remove it.
*   **Freshness of White Pepper:** White pepper loses its potency over time. For the best heat, use freshly ground white pepper or a relatively new container.
*   **Egg Drop Technique:** Pour the beaten egg in a very thin stream while gently stirring the soup. This creates delicate, feathery egg ribbons rather than large clumps.
*   **Mushrooms Galore:** Don't skimp on the mushrooms! Wood ear and shiitake mushrooms provide essential texture and umami depth that is characteristic of a great Hot and Sour Soup.

## Serving Suggestions & Pairings

Hot and Sour Soup is incredibly versatile. It can be enjoyed as a hearty appetizer, a light lunch, or as part of a larger Chinese feast.

*   **As an Appetizer:** It's a fantastic starter for any Chinese meal, whetting the appetite without being too heavy.
*   **Light Meal:** Paired with some steamed rice, a simple green salad, or a few spring rolls, a bowl of Hot and Sour Soup makes for a satisfying and flavorful light lunch or dinner.
*   **Alongside Mains:** It complements a wide range of Chinese dishes, from Kung Pao Chicken to Mapo Tofu, as its distinct flavors offer a refreshing contrast.
*   **Beverage Pairings:** A light lager, jasmine tea, or even a crisp white wine like a Sauvignon Blanc can pair beautifully with the soup's bold flavors.

## Variations: Vegetarian & More

The classic Hot and Sour Soup is wonderfully adaptable, allowing for numerous delicious variations:

*   **Vegetarian/Vegan Hot and Sour Soup:** Easily made vegetarian by using vegetable broth and omitting the pork. For a vegan version, also ensure your black vinegar is vegan-friendly (most are) and skip the egg drop. You can increase the amount of tofu or add other vegetables like shredded carrots, water chestnuts, or even firm eggplant for more texture.
*   **Seafood Hot and Sour Soup:** Incorporate shrimp, scallops, or thin slices of fish for a delightful seafood twist. Add them towards the end of cooking so they don't overcook.
*   **Spicier Versions:** For those who crave more heat, a dash of chili flakes or a spoonful of chili oil can be added to the broth or served on the side. Some recipes also include fermented chili bean paste (*doubanjiang*) for a deeper, more complex spice.
*   **Regional Differences:** While Sichuan is known for its spicy and numbing flavors, other regions might have slightly different takes. For example, some Cantonese versions might be milder and sweeter, while Taiwanese versions might incorporate more local ingredients.

From its humble beginnings to its status as a global favorite, Hot and Sour Soup continues to captivate palates with its dynamic flavors and comforting warmth. This guide provides all you need to recreate this Chinese culinary masterpiece in your own kitchen. Don't hesitate to experiment with the levels of heat and sourness to find your perfect balance. Enjoy the journey of crafting this iconic dish, and savor every spoonful of your homemade Hot and Sour Soup!
